objects.description: Enumeration of supported PCM sample formats for the encoder API. Values indicate signed 16/24/32-bit little-endian PCM and 32-bit float. Used when initializing the encoder to specify input PCM format.
Opaque handle type for the LDAC encoder instance. The underlying struct is not defined in this header; treat this as a managed opaque pointer obtained and released via the provided API.
Opaque handle type for the LDAC Adaptive Bit Rate (ABR) controller instance. The underlying struct is not defined in this header; obtain and release via the ABR API.

functions.name: ldacBT_get_handle
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new LDAC encoder handle for use with the LDAC encode APIs. Use this before any other ldacBT_* calls that require a handle. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: None beyond standard memory availability.
Caller must later release the handle with ldacBT_free_handle() when no longer needed.

functions.name: ldacBT_free_handle
functions.description: Releases an LDAC encoder handle and associated resources. After this call, the handle must not be used.
requirements: hLdacBt must be a valid LDAC handle previously obtained from ldacBT_get_handle().
hLdacBt must not be used after this call.
If the handle was initialized, it does not need to be explicitly closed before freeing (not stated but safe to assume release covers resources).

functions.name: ldacBT_close_handle
functions.description: Closes an initialized LDAC handle, releasing internal encoder state while keeping the handle reusable. The handle can be re-initialized again via ldacBT_init_handle_encode().
requirements: hLdacBt must be a valid, initialized LDAC handle.
Call ldacBT_init_handle_encode() again before encoding after closing.

functions.name: ldacBT_get_version
functions.description: Returns the library version as an integer encoded as: bits 23-16 major, 15-8 minor, 7-0 branch. Example: 0x00010203 -> 1.02.03.
requirements: None.

functions.name: ldacBT_get_sampling_freq
functions.description: Returns the current sampling frequency configured in the LDAC encoder handle, or -1 on failure.
requirements: hLdacBt must be a valid LDAC handle initialized via ldacBT_init_handle_encode() before calling.

functions.name: ldacBT_get_bitrate
functions.description: Returns the bitrate (in bps) for the previously processed LDAC transport frame for the given handle, or -1 on failure.
requirements: hLdacBt must be a valid LDAC handle initialized via ldacBT_init_handle_encode() before calling.

functions.name: ldacBT_init_handle_encode
functions.signature: int ldacBT_init_handle_encode(HANDLE_LDAC_BT hLdacBt, int mtu, int eqmid, int cm, LDACBT_SMPL_FMT_T fmt, int sf)
functions.description: Initializes an LDAC handle for encoding with the given MTU, Encode Quality Mode Index (EQMID), channel mode, input PCM format, and sampling frequency. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure. Re-initialize if mtu, cm, or sf changes.
requirements: hLdacBt must be allocated via ldacBT_get_handle() prior to calling.
mtu must be set to the MTU size (in bytes) of the AVDTP transport channel used for transmission.
eqmid must be a valid Encode Quality Mode Index (e.g., LDACBT_EQMID_HQ, LDACBT_EQMID_SQ, LDACBT_EQMID_MQ, or LDACBT_EQMID_ABR as appropriate).
cm must be a valid LDAC Bluetooth A2DP channel mode (e.g., MONO/DUAL CHANNEL/STEREO per LDAC).
fmt must be one of LDACBT_SMPL_FMT_S16, LDACBT_SMPL_FMT_S24, LDACBT_SMPL_FMT_S32, or LDACBT_SMPL_FMT_F32.
sf must be a supported sampling frequency (44.1, 48, 88.2, or 96 kHz as per library support).
If mtu, cm, or sf changes after initialization, the handle must be re-initialized by calling this function again before further encoding.

functions.name: ldacBT_set_eqmid
functions.description: Sets the Encode Quality Mode Index (EQMID) for an initialized LDAC encoder handle. Can be called any time after initialization. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.
requirements: hLdacBt must be initialized via ldacBT_init_handle_encode() before calling.
eqmid must be a valid EQMID value.

functions.name: ldacBT_get_eqmid
functions.description: Gets the currently configured Encode Quality Mode Index (EQMID) for the given handle. Returns the EQMID on success or -1 on failure.
requirements: hLdacBt must be initialized via ldacBT_init_handle_encode() before calling.

functions.name: ldacBT_alter_eqmid_priority
functions.description: Adjusts the EQMID by one step toward either higher quality or better connection robustness. Use LDACBT_EQMID_INC_QUALITY (+1) to move toward LDACBT_EQMID_HQ, or LDACBT_EQMID_INC_CONNECTION (-1) to move away from HQ. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure. To restore a prescribed EQMID, call ldacBT_init_handle_encode() or ldacBT_set_eqmid().
requirements: hLdacBt must be initialized via ldacBT_init_handle_encode() before calling.
priority must be LDACBT_EQMID_INC_QUALITY (1) or LDACBT_EQMID_INC_CONNECTION (-1).
Caller should be aware that states other than the previously prescribed EQMID may result after adjustment; explicitly set EQMID again to restore if needed.

functions.name: ldacBT_encode
functions.signature: int ldacBT_encode(HANDLE_LDAC_BT hLdacBt, void *p_pcm, int *pcm_used, unsigned char *p_stream, int *stream_sz, int *frame_num)
functions.description: Encodes PCM audio to LDAC transport frames. Input is 128 samples per channel per call (or zero-padded if fewer). Output LDAC transport frames are written to p_stream when available; not every call yields output. Set p_pcm to NULL to finalize and flush remaining data. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.
requirements: hLdacBt must be initialized via ldacBT_init_handle_encode() before calling.
Input PCM must be interleaved by 1 sample (e.g., L0,R0,L1,R1,...) and match the format configured in ldacBT_init_handle_encode().
Each encode step expects 128 samples per channel; if fewer are available, the unused region in the input buffer must be zero-filled.
p_pcm may be NULL to trigger finalize/flush processing.
pcm_used must be a valid pointer; on return it receives total referenced PCM size in bytes (NumSamples * NumChannels * sizeof(sample)).
p_stream must be a valid buffer pointer; stream_sz must be a valid pointer to receive the output byte count; frame_num must be a valid pointer to receive the number of output LDAC transport frames.
Output availability is not guaranteed on every call; check that *stream_sz > 0 to determine presence of output (the docs describe checking if positive).
Encoded output size is bounded by the configured MTU; ensure p_stream is large enough for that MTU.

functions.name: ldacBT_get_error_code
functions.description: Returns the most recently established error code for the given LDAC handle. Use provided macros LDACBT_FATAL(), LDACBT_ERROR(), LDACBT_HANDLE_ERR(), and LDACBT_BLOCK_ERR() to interpret it.
requirements: hLdacBt must be a valid LDAC handle allocated via ldacBT_get_handle().

functions.name: ldac_ABR_get_handle
functions.description: Allocates and returns a new LDAC ABR (Adaptive Bit Rate) handle used to manage bitrate adaptation based on TX queue depth. Returns NULL on failure.
requirements: None beyond standard memory availability.
Caller must later release the handle with ldac_ABR_free_handle().

functions.name: ldac_ABR_free_handle
functions.description: Releases an LDAC ABR handle and its resources. After this call, the ABR handle must not be used.
requirements: hLdacAbr must be a valid ABR handle previously obtained from ldac_ABR_get_handle().
hLdacAbr must not be used after this call.

functions.name: ldac_ABR_Init
functions.signature: int ldac_ABR_Init(HANDLE_LDAC_ABR hLdacAbr, unsigned int interval_ms)
functions.description: Initializes an LDAC ABR handle and sets the interval (in milliseconds) at which ldac_ABR_Proc() should be called. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.
requirements: hLdacAbr must be a valid ABR handle obtained from ldac_ABR_get_handle().
interval_ms must be within 1 ms to 500 ms (inclusive).
The interval should be as short as possible when no packet accumulation occurs and radio conditions are good (guidance).
Reinitialize by calling ldac_ABR_Init() again when TX queue state changes greatly (e.g., queue cleared).

functions.name: ldac_ABR_set_thresholds
functions.signature: int ldac_ABR_set_thresholds(HANDLE_LDAC_ABR hLdacAbr, unsigned int thCritical, unsigned int thDangerousTrend, unsigned int thSafety4HQSQ)
functions.description: Configures ABR thresholds that govern bitrate adjustments based on TX queue depth. Returns 0 on success or -1 on failure.
requirements: hLdacAbr must be a valid ABR handle.
thCritical, thDangerousTrend, and thSafety4HQSQ must each be greater than 0.
Thresholds represent the number of packets stored in the TX queue.
Thresholds must satisfy thCritical >= thDangerousTrend >= thSafety4HQSQ.

functions.name: ldac_ABR_Proc
functions.signature: int ldac_ABR_Proc(HANDLE_LDAC_BT hLdacBt, HANDLE_LDAC_ABR hLdacAbr, unsigned int TxQueueDepth, unsigned int flagEnable)
functions.description: ABR main processing step. Should be called periodically at the interval set by ldac_ABR_Init(). Updates internal ABR state and, if enabled, adjusts LDAC encoder EQMID based on TX queue depth. Returns the updated EQMID on success, or -1 on failure.
requirements: hLdacBt must be a valid LDAC handle.
hLdacAbr must be a valid ABR handle initialized via ldac_ABR_Init().
Call this function at the configured interval even when flagEnable is 0.
TxQueueDepth must be the current depth (in packets) of the TX queue.
flagEnable controls whether ABR is allowed to adjust the LDAC encode bitrate (1 = allowed, 0 = not allowed).

data_types.description: Arbitrary binary data interpreted as interleaved PCM sample bytes for audio encoding. The buffer length corresponds to 128 samples per channel times the number of channels times bytes-per-sample. The byte layout must match the configured PCM format (S16/S24/S32 little-endian integers or 32-bit IEEE float) and channel interleaving by single samples (e.g., L0,R0,L1,R1,...). Any content is accepted by the fuzzer, but the function expects these bytes to represent PCM audio frames.
